strings.name: Jensen Huang
strings.summary: Jensen Huang co-founded NVIDIA after moving from Taiwan to the United States and training in electrical engineering. The team he led began with graphics chips for personal computers and gradually expanded GPUs into important tools for scientific computing and artificial intelligence. The CUDA software ecosystem, deep-learning computation and data-center platforms are central to understanding his influence on the industry.
strings.coverageNote: This edition focuses on education, entrepreneurship and technology development from 1963 to 2024; historical positions are not presented as live employment information. Sources differ on his birth city, so only Taiwan is specified.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Co-founding NVIDIA
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Founded NVIDIA in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Advancing general-purpose GPU computing
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The company announced the CUDA architecture in 2006, opening GPU parallel-computing capabilities to researchers and developers.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Artificial intelligence infrastructure
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: From supporting AlexNet training to introducing Blackwell, helped expand the use of GPUs in deep learning.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Introduces the Blackwell platform
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Presented a new generation of GPU platforms for generative AI and accelerated computing at GTC.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Real-time ray tracing joins the product range
strings.timeline.event-02.text: NVIDIA introduced RTX technology, expanding the applications of real-time computer graphics rendering.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: GPUs support a deep-learning breakthrough
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The AlexNet neural network was trained using NVIDIA GPUs, becoming a landmark in deep-learning development.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Announces the CUDA architecture
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Extended GPU parallel processing beyond graphics, laying foundations for scientific computing and the later AI ecosystem.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: GPUs become a central product direction
strings.timeline.event-05.text: NVIDIA made graphics processors a core product focus, advancing graphics computing on personal computers.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Starts a company with two partners
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Founded NVIDIA with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, targeting 3D graphics for gaming and multimedia.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Receives a master’s degree from Stanford
strings.timeline.event-07.text: After completing his undergraduate studies and entering the chip industry, earned a master’s degree in electrical engineering from Stanford.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes his electrical engineering degree
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Graduated from Oregon State University and worked at AMD and LSI Logic early in his career.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Taiwan
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Lived in Asia during childhood before moving to the United States; his education and career spanned Asia and North America.
